title: Privacy Settings
about: Choose who sees your posts and who can reach you.

cards.prompt: Sam's account is public. **Flip a switch** and watch what strangers can see.
cards.explanation: Each switch hides one thing from strangers.

cards.prompt: Messages are now friends only. A stranger taps Send. **What happens?**

image.alt: Left: Sam's settings, with the switch Messages: friends only being turned on. Right: a stranger's phone on PixelFox's profile, typing hey, cool tricks, with a finger on Send. Below it, a question mark.
image.revealAlt: The stranger's Send button is greyed out, with a note: PixelFox only gets messages from friends.

cards.explanation: With friends-only messages, people Sam hasn't added can't message Sam.

cards.title: Privacy settings
cards.body: **Privacy settings** choose who can see your posts and who can reach you. Each switch controls one thing.

image.alt: Sam's settings with four switches, each labelled with the one thing it controls: Private account (on) controls posts, Messages: friends only (on) controls messages, Share location (off) controls location, and Review tags (on) controls tags.

cards.prompt: Jo tagged Sam in a photo outside school. **Tap the switch** that lets Sam OK tags first.

image.alt: Top: a photo Jo tagged Sam in, outside the school gate, two kids from behind: Tagged by Jo, shows on Sam's profile. Below: Sam's four switches, all off: Private account, Messages: friends only, Share location, Review tags.
image.revealAlt: Review tags is now on. The tagged photo is greyed out: Waiting for Sam's OK.

options.nudge: Which switch is about photos other people tag you in?
Which switch is about photos other people tag you in?
Which switch is about photos other people tag you in?

cards.explanation: Review tags keeps photos Sam's tagged in off Sam's profile until Sam says OK.
cards.showAnswer: Review tags: tagged photos wait for Sam's OK before they show on Sam's profile.

cards.prompt: Sam's game friend asks for Sam's school and a photo. **Tap what Sam should do.**

image.alt: A chat on Sam's phone with GameMate_8, a game-controller picture with no face, marked Friend. Their message: what school do u go to? send a pic! The chat's menu is open, showing Block and Report.
image.revealAlt: The chat with GameMate_8 is closed, marked Reported and Blocked. Sam stands beside a grown-up at home and says: Can I show you something?

options.nudge: GameMate_8 is already Sam's friend: would a private account keep them out?

options.text: Send a photo, not the school
options.nudge: Think back to the front-steps photo: what can a photo give away?

options.text: Report, block, tell a trusted adult

cards.explanation: Settings can't keep out someone Sam already let in, so report, block and tell a trusted adult.
cards.showAnswer: Report, block and tell a trusted adult: it's not Sam's fault, and telling someone keeps Sam safe.

cards.prompt: Your account is private. A follower screenshots your post. **Tap what can stop them sharing it.**

image.alt: Left: your settings with Private account switched on and a padlock. Right: a follower's phone with your post, a white screenshot flash and a camera badge, and a Share arrow lifting off.
image.revealAlt: The screenshot of your post has spread to three more phones, joined by a trail of footprints labelled digital footprint.

options.nudge: Think back to the friends' phones in the last lesson: what could they do with a post?
Think back to the friends' phones in the last lesson: what could they do with a post?

options.text: No setting: followers can copy it

cards.explanation: Settings choose who sees a post, but a follower can still copy it, so post like anyone might see.
cards.showAnswer: No setting stops it: a follower can still copy your post, so share only what you'd be OK with anyone seeing.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
**Privacy settings** choose who sees and reaches you. If someone crosses the line, **report, block and tell a trusted adult**.

**Try this:** Open one of your accounts' privacy settings and turn on "Private account".

**Next:** Why a torch app wants your contacts, and how to say no.
